Headline: HUD Work Requirement & Time Limit Proposed Rule Threatens 3.7M Households
Summary: HUD proposed rule lets PHAs and Section 8/public housing owners impose up to 40hr/week work requirements and time limits as short as 2 years; comment period closed May 1 2026; final rule pending; litigation expected.
Action_Required: Attorney Review; Model PET/TCAP as HUD-independent revenue stream
Internal_Notes: If NYCHA or voucher holders lose federal assistance, PET equity accrual must not be contingent on continued federal subsidy receipt
Proposed_Redline_Text: ADD: 'Eligibility for equity accrual shall not be terminated solely due to loss of federal rental assistance resulting from HUD work-requirement or time-limit rules; the City shall provide a bridge subsidy drawn from reallocated HPD/HRA funds for up to 12 months.'

Headline: RGB Approves First-Ever 0% Freeze on 1- and 2-Year Leases
Summary: NYC RGB voted 7-1 for historic 0% increase on both 1- and 2-year rent-stabilized leases effective Oct 1 2026–Sept 30 2027; landlords warn of distress and litigation.
Action_Required: Attorney Review; decouple PET equity calculation from RGB baseline
Internal_Notes: Frozen legal rents change baseline calculations for any PET equity-conversion formula tied to rent rolls
Proposed_Redline_Text: ADD: 'Equity contribution values shall be calculated independent of annual RGB determinations using a fixed baseline adjusted only by AMI index to insulate the Program from RGB volatility and potential legal challenge to the freeze order.'

Headline: Mamdani Unveils $28B Block by Block Housing Plan
Summary: Mayor Mamdani's plan targets 200000 new affordable units + 200000 preserved over 10 years; $22B new investment; $5.6B for NYCHA; $40/hr construction minimum wage; relaxed prefab regulations.
Action_Required: CFO and Attorney Review; align PET fiscal ask with $70B Ten-Year Capital Plan bonding structure
Internal_Notes: PET must be framed as self-amortizing complement to Block by Block, not a competing budget ask
Proposed_Redline_Text: ADD: 'This Framework is designed to operate as a self-amortizing complement to the City Ten-Year Capital Plan and Block by Block housing initiative, generating recoverable public equity rather than requiring new net capital appropriation.'

Headline: Adopted Summary of Guidelines 2026-27
Summary: Official adopted RGB order confirming 0% guideline for one- and two-year leases and 49% vacancy allowance for decontrolled/MBR units effective Sept 30 2026.
Action_Required: Attorney Review; verify PET does not rely on vacancy allowance mechanics
Internal_Notes: 49% vacancy bonus could incentivize landlord turnover churn that TCAP acquisition model should account for as acquisition-timing risk
Redline_Section: TCAP Bill C, Acquisition Trigger Section
Proposed_Redline_Text: ADD: 'Acquisition-trigger eligibility shall include buildings where owners exercise the Special Guideline vacancy allowance more than twice within a 24-month period as a proxy indicator of displacement risk warranting TCAP outreach.'

Headline: NYC CCHR Opposes Federal Rollback of Equal Access Housing Protections
Summary: CCHR formally opposed Trump Administration proposal to roll back Equal Access housing nondiscrimination protections (disability/gender identity) on July 14 2026 citing conflict with NYC Human Rights Law.
Action_Required: Attorney Review; ensure PET nondiscrimination clauses exceed any weakened federal floor
Internal_Notes: Federal rollback creates gap-filling need; PET eligibility must explicitly codify NYC Human Rights Law protections
Proposed_Redline_Text: ADD: 'Nondiscrimination protections under this Program are established independently under NYC Human Rights Law (Title 8 NYC Admin Code) and shall remain in full effect regardless of any narrowing of federal Equal Access or HUD nondiscrimination regulations.'

Headline: Chelsea NYCHA Section 9-to-8 Conversion Gets Federal Greenlight Amid Litigation
Summary: HUD reaffirmed approval for NYCHA Fulton/Elliott-Chelsea conversion from public housing to Section 8 via PACT/RAD enabling demolition/rebuild of 2056 units plus 3500 mixed-income units; tenant rights litigation ongoing.
Action_Required: Program Manager Review; TCAP should assert right-of-first-refusal at Section 9-to-8 conversion sites
Internal_Notes: Section 9-to-8 conversions shift long-term public asset control to private partners; TCAP must assert right-of-first-refusal at conversion sites
Redline_Section: TCAP Bill B, Sec. 4 (Right of First Refusal)
Proposed_Redline_Text: ADD: 'The Right of First Refusal established herein shall extend to NYCHA properties undergoing Section 9-to-Section 8 conversion (RAD/PACT or successor programs) granting qualifying tenant associations the option to pursue cooperative acquisition in lieu of private third-party ownership transfer.'

Headline: Comptroller Levine Blasts NY Rent Policies for Housing Crisis
Summary: NYC Comptroller Mark Levine criticized state and city rent regulations as worsening the housing supply crisis arguing regulatory approach alone will not solve affordability.
Action_Required: Program Manager Review; prepare rebuttal framing PET as supply-neutral equity tool, not rent control
Internal_Notes: Levine's critique could be weaponized against PET; reframe PET messaging as ROI-positive, not rent suppression
Proposed_Redline_Text: ADD: 'This Framework operates independently of rent regulation policy and is designed to generate fiscal ROI through equity accrual rather than rent suppression, addressing critiques that regulatory-only approaches fail to expand supply.'

Headline: NYCHA FY2027 Draft Annual Plan Public Hearing July 29 2026
Summary: NYCHA holds hybrid public hearing July 29 2026 on FY2027 Draft Annual Plan; written comments accepted through August 1 2026 — direct advocacy window for PET/TCAP alignment with NYCHA capital planning.
Action_Required: Program Manager Action: Draft and submit public comment before Aug 1 deadline
Internal_Notes: Time-sensitive advocacy opportunity to align PET funding reuse strategy with NYCHA FY27 plan before finalization
Proposed_Redline_Text: DRAFT PUBLIC COMMENT: Request NYCHA FY2027 Annual Plan explicitly reference compatibility with Tenant Coop Acquisition Program (TCAP) for Preservation Trust and RAD/PACT conversion sites.

Headline: 2026 NYC Worst Landlord Watchlist Released
Summary: Public Advocate's watchlist names A&E Real Estate's Margaret Brunn and Donald Hastings as top offenders with ~9000 combined violations spotlighting chronic disinvestment landlords as prime TCAP acquisition targets.
Action_Required: Program Manager Review: cross-reference Watchlist addresses against TCAP target-building list
Internal_Notes: Watchlist provides ready-made politically legitimate target list for TCAP distressed-building acquisition pipeline
Redline_Section: TCAP Bill A, Sec. 2 (Priority Acquisition Criteria)
Proposed_Redline_Text: ADD: 'Priority acquisition status shall be automatically conferred upon buildings whose owners appear on the NYC Public Advocate's Annual Worst Landlord Watchlist subject to tenant association consent.'

Headline: Mamdani Administration Closes Financing on Sol on Park (229 Affordable Senior Homes)
Summary: City closed financing on Sol on Park converting NYCHA Morris Houses campus land into 229 affordable senior units — live model of public land leverage relevant to PET Public Land for Public Good provisions.
Action_Required: Monitor: use as precedent citation in PET public-land sections
Internal_Notes: Useful precedent/ROI comparison case for PET fiscal modeling of public-land-leverage deals
Redline_Section: PETF Sec. 6 (Public Land for Public Good)
Proposed_Redline_Text: ADD (citation only): 'See Sol on Park financial closing (NYCHA Morris Houses campus July 2026) as precedent model for senior-focused public-land equity development.'

Headline: Opinion: Housing Lottery Promised Stability Then Rent Went Up
Summary: Op-ed argues affordable housing lottery units under prior RGB increases eroded promised stability — cautionary tale for PET/TCAP messaging around long-term affordability guarantees.
Action_Required: Program Manager Monitor: no immediate legal action required
Internal_Notes: Reputational/messaging risk: PET must explicitly guarantee durability of affordability beyond initial subsidy period
Proposed_Redline_Text: CONSIDERATION: Evaluate adding a permanent in-perpetuity deed restriction clause rather than time-limited affordability covenant given public criticism of lottery unit rent creep.
